what_matters.head: MAS left its Singapore-dollar policy unchanged this morning. All 10 analysts in a Reuters poll last week had expected it to tighten again, after a very slight tightening in July.
what_matters.detail: MAS kept the slope, width and centre of its policy band. It expects core inflation to stay slightly elevated in the coming quarters and to ease from mid-2027: 1.5–2.0% for 2026 and 1.5–2.5% for 2027. Singapore's economy grew 5.4% from a year earlier in the third quarter (advance estimate), led by technology.

what_matters.head: US consumer prices for September are due at 20:30 SGT tonight. TSMC reports on Thursday at 14:00 SGT, and US producer prices follow at 20:30.
what_matters.detail: Reuters reported that economists expect consumer prices to have risen 0.6% in September, after 0.4% in August, and 3.6% from a year earlier, up from 3.4%. TSMC's forecast and the options-implied move are under Earnings.

latest.tape_note: US stocks were flat on Tuesday: the S&P 500 was little changed, the Nasdaq slipped 0.2% and the Dow 0.4%. JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo and Citigroup opened the results season, and all four closed lower, Citigroup by about 5.5%. Memory-chip stocks fell for a second day on CXMT's news, and the Philadelphia chip index fell for a fifth straight day, only slightly on Tuesday. The US dollar index fell 0.4%, a little more than its usual day, after New York Fed President John Williams said he still expects one more rate hike this year but sees no need for more in 2027. The 10-year Treasury yield slipped 2 basis points to 5.22%, and oil rose 0.4%. The US dollar fell 0.1% against the Singapore dollar.
latest.tonight: US consumer prices for September at 20:30 SGT. Another 8.9% tranche of Cerebras shares held under its IPO lock-up becomes free to sell today. The OCP Global Summit in San Jose runs until Thursday.
